content.value_statement: Building Azure Maps features in .NET requires choosing several prerelease SDKs and authentication patterns. This skill provides focused examples for search, routing, rendering, geolocation, weather, and error handling.
actual_capabilities: Explains package installation and authentication with subscription keys, Microsoft Entra ID, and shared access signatures.
Shows address geocoding, batch geocoding, reverse geocoding, and boundary polygon retrieval.
Covers route directions, traffic options, route matrices, and reachable-range calculations.
Demonstrates map tile retrieval and file output with the rendering client.
Provides examples for IP country lookup and current weather conditions.
Summarizes important SDK types, rate-limit handling, caching, and request error handling.
limitations: Examples reference prerelease SDK versions that may change.
The skill does not execute requests, provision resources, or validate your Azure configuration.
An Azure Maps account, credentials, network access, and applicable service quota are required.
Production applications need additional retries, observability, input validation, privacy controls, and cost management.

use_cases.title: Add Address Search
use_cases.description: Create a .NET address lookup flow with confidence checks and reverse geocoding.

use_cases.title: Plan Delivery Routes
use_cases.description: Design directions and route-matrix requests for multiple origins and destinations.

use_cases.title: Build Location Dashboards
use_cases.description: Combine map tiles, IP country lookup, and weather data for operational views.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Authentication
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to configure Azure Maps Search in a .NET project using Microsoft Entra ID. Include required packages, settings, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Geocoding Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a C# workflow that geocodes an address and checks result confidence. Explain error handling for invalid input, authentication failure, and rate limits.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Route Matrix
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a .NET route matrix for these origins and destinations: [locations]. Choose synchronous or asynchronous processing and explain the service limits.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Production Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Azure Maps .NET design: [design]. Recommend authentication, caching, retries, privacy controls, monitoring, quota management, and tests for each workflow.

output_examples.input: Plan a secure .NET address search using Microsoft Entra ID.
output: Recommended authentication: use the default Azure credential with the Azure Maps client identifier.
Flow: create the search client, submit the address, and inspect confidence before storing coordinates.
Checks: handle authentication failures, rate limits, ambiguous results, and missing coordinates.

output_examples.input: Choose a route matrix approach for 40 origins and 12 destinations.
output: Use the asynchronous matrix operation because the synchronous workflow supports at most 100 combinations.
Add polling limits, partial-result handling, retries, and quota monitoring.

output_examples.input: Outline a map tile download workflow for a location dashboard.
output: Convert longitude and latitude into a tile index using the chosen zoom and tile size.
Request the required imagery tile and stream the response to controlled storage.
Cache stable tiles and retain the required copyright information.

best_practices: Prefer Microsoft Entra ID for production and keep subscription keys outside source control.
Batch requests when appropriate, cache stable results, and apply bounded exponential backoff for rate limits.
Validate coordinate order, user input, service limits, response confidence, and regional availability before using results.
anti_patterns: Do not embed subscription keys, shared access signatures, or client secrets in code or prompts.
Do not use synchronous route matrices above documented combination limits.
Do not treat sample code as production-ready without testing current SDK versions, quotas, failure modes, and privacy requirements.

faq.question: Does this skill run Azure Maps commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides documentation and examples that you adapt and run in your own .NET environment.

faq.question: Which authentication method should production applications use?
faq.answer: Use Microsoft Entra ID with managed identity or another appropriate default Azure credential when your environment supports it.

faq.question: Can I use an Azure Maps subscription key?
faq.answer: Yes. Store it in a protected configuration source and rotate it according to your security policy.

faq.question: Are the listed SDK versions stable?
faq.answer: Several listed packages are prerelease versions. Verify package versions and API signatures against current Microsoft documentation.

faq.question: Which Azure Maps workflows are covered?
faq.answer: The guidance covers search, routing, rendering, IP geolocation, weather, authentication, and basic request error handling.

faq.question: What should I validate before deployment?
faq.answer: Validate SDK compatibility, coordinate order, quotas, retries, regional availability, pricing, privacy obligations, and credential permissions.
